To guard our heart means to be vigilant over what we allow into our awareness, refusing to entertain thoughts that are false, evil, or negative. When our hearts and minds are fixed on the Truth, on YHWH, we live in holiness.

● Practical Application: Continually return your attention to God. Speak YHWH's name, and let the light of His Word fill your mind. As the Apostle Paul advises, "Whatsoever things are true... think on these things" (Philippians 4:8, Ethiopian KJV). Fill your heart with divine truth, and there will be no room for sin or deception.
3. The Way: Prayer in Secret and Sincerity

Jesus modeled and taught the importance of private, sincere prayer, saying, "But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret" (Matthew 6:6, Ethiopian KJV). Prayer is the way in which we commune with God, aligning our desires with His will. The key to effective prayer is humility, sincerity, and faith.

● Practical Application: Follow the principles of proper prayer by finding a private place to pray daily, free from distractions. When you pray, speak to the Father in secret, aligning your heart with His will. As it is written, "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you" (Matthew 7:7, Ethiopian KJV). Believe that what you ask in faith will be granted, knowing that your requests align with God's greater purpose​​​.
4. The Flow: Divine Love and Compassion

Divine love, or The Flow, is not merely an emotional feeling but the eternal essence of God's nature. It purifies, heals, and sustains all creation. As Christ exemplified, this love is sacrificial and unconditioned, washing away all sins. Compassion flows from this love, allowing us to give without burden or hesitation, for "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends" (John 15:13, Ethiopian KJV).

● Practical Application: Open yourself to divine love in prayer and allow it to overflow into your interactions with others. Let compassion be a natural, effortless expression of God's love, which heals and restores. True compassion is born from divine love, not from human effort.
5. The View: A Vision of Divine Unity

Holiness is seeing God in all things, and seeing all things through God. Jesus said, "The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light" (Matthew 6:22, Ethiopian KJV). This "single eye" is the divine vision—the awareness of God's presence in every aspect of life.

● Practical Application: Develop spiritual vision by continually asking yourself, "Am I aware of God's presence in this moment?" The more you align your awareness with divine reality, the more you will see the world through the eyes of Christ.
6. The Hope: Purity and Perfection in Christ

Our hope is to be made perfect in Christ, and this perfection comes through the purification of the heart. Jesus commanded, "Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect" (Matthew 5:48, Ethiopian KJV). This call to perfection is not about moral striving, but about aligning our hearts with God's love, allowing His purity to transform us.
● Practical Application: Focus on Christ's light and perfection daily, and seek to purify your thoughts, words, and actions. Through this hope, we are continually made more like Him.
7. The One: Union with the Father

To be holy is to be one with God, as Jesus prayed, "That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us" (John 17:21, Ethiopian KJV). This union is the ultimate goal of holiness—complete oneness with the Father, where our will and His will become one.
● Practical Application: Seek this union through daily prayer and meditation on Christ's words. The closer we align ourselves with God's will, the more we experience divine oneness.
8. The Law: As Within, So Without

The law of holiness is that what is within us manifests outwardly. As Jesus taught, "For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh" (Matthew 12:34, Ethiopian KJV). When our hearts are filled with the Word of God, our actions naturally reflect His will.

● Practical Application: Continually examine the contents of your heart and ensure that it is filled with truth, love, and light. As you align your inner life with God, your outer life will reflect His kingdom.
9. The Son: The Embodiment of Divine Love

Jesus Christ is the ultimate embodiment of divine love in human form. Through His life, death, and resurrection, He showed us the way to live in holiness. "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me" (John 14:6, Ethiopian KJV). To follow Christ is to embody His love, allowing it to flow through us as we become more like Him.
● Practical Application: Follow Christ's example by keeping His words in your heart and living according to His teachings. As you do, you will reflect the Son's divine love in all that you do.
Closing Thoughts:

Holiness is a journey of becoming more like Christ through surrender, prayer, love, and unity with God. As you follow these principles, you will grow in spiritual maturity, embodying the life, truth, and way of Jesus Christ. Continue this journey into deeper communion with God through prayer, as it is the foundation of our relationship with Him.
B: The Path: Understanding Agnosis, Self-Gnosis, and Gnosis
Agnosis represents ignorance of divine truth—a disconnection from God's presence, where the individual is unaware of their true relationship with God and is led by ego and material desires.
Self-Gnosis refers to the transition where one begins to awaken to the divine knowledge of being a son or daughter of God. Through practicing eternal truths, one aligns with divine will.

Gnosis, however, is the culmination of this spiritual journey, where one fully embodies divine knowledge—not only of the Self but of the entire divine order of creation. In Gnosis, an individual transcends mere intellectual understanding and becomes fully aligned with the Eternal Mirror, reflecting God the Father and His children.

Aspect|One Who Lives in Agnosis (Ignorance)|One Who Is Transitioning (Self-Gnosis)|One Who Lives in Gnosis (Attained Divine Knowledge)|

The Truth (Abiding in the Word)|(Ignorance of the Word): Unaware of the divine truth, disconnected from the resonance of God's name and presence.|(Awakening to the Word): Acknowledges divine truth but struggles to consistently align with it. Hears God's voice intermittently.|(Living in the Truth): Abides constantly in the Word. Practices divine breath (Yah-Weh) and harmonizes with the resonance of God's presence.|

2. The Flow (Living in the Spirit)|(Disconnected from the Spirit): Unaware of the divine flow, relying on personal will rather than God's guidance.|(Engaging with the Flow): Experiences moments of divine flow but struggles with consistency, often losing the connection in daily life.|(Living in the Flow): Engages daily with the Holy Spirit through breath and the Flow, experiencing inner calm and divine peace in all actions.|

3. The View (Childlike Awareness)|(Material vision): Perceives the world through a materialistic lens, disconnected from the divine reality behind creation.|(Beginning to see God): Starts to perceive God's presence but often defaults to ego-driven perspectives and worldviews.|(Spiritual clarity): Cultivates childlike awareness, observing God's hand in all things, free from intellectual interference, and seeing through the soul.|

4. The Life (Spiritual Rebirth)|(Dominated by ego): Struggles for control, restless, and resists surrendering personal will to God.|(Learning to surrender): Practices surrendering but often returns to old habits of ego and personal desires.|(Living in spiritual rebirth): Dies to self daily, surrendering to God's will fully, and experiences renewal of life and clarity in His presence.|

5. The Way (Proper Prayer)|(Disconnected from prayer): Prays for material desires or does not engage in prayer with God the Father.|(Learning to pray): Begins integrating proper prayer, often focused on personal desires, while struggling to fully trust God's timing.|(Embodied prayer): Prays in private, submitting entirely to God's will. Uses the Lord's Prayer and focuses on aligning with divine guidance.|

6. The Hope (Hopeful Repentance)|(Lack of hope): Relies on worldly hope, feeling disconnected from the divine plan and purpose.|(Hoping for divine guidance): Experiences fluctuations between doubt and hope, struggling to hold a consistent vision of divine perfection.|(Living in hope): Focuses on the vision of divine perfection, trusting in repentance, and actively living with the expectation of spiritual fulfillment.|

7. The One (Righteous Perseverance)|(Lacks perseverance): Easily discouraged by trials, seeks worldly solutions, and avoids spiritual growth.|(Persevering in faith): Demonstrates perseverance in some areas but inconsistently seeks the deeper revelation of God's will.|(Perfection of the One): Seeks God continually, receives the Holy Anointing, and attains the revelation of God the Father, seeing Him clearly in all things.|

8. The Law (Divine Law and Karma)|(Disregard for the law): Ignores or breaks divine law, resulting in inner conflict, dissatisfaction, and spiritual disconnection.|(Learning to follow the law): Struggles with keeping the commandments, occasionally slipping back into old habits or temptations.|(Mastery of the law): Lives in harmony with divine law. Understands that "Do unto others as you would have them do unto you" reflects life as a mirror.|

9. The Son (Becoming Like Christ)|(Disconnected from sonship): Acts from ego, disconnected from divine purpose, and unaware of being a child of God.|(Recognizing divine sonship): Begins to understand the calling to serve but struggles with ego and attachments to worldly identity.|(Perfection of the Son): Meets Christ directly, becomes like Him, and understands the role of judging angels as a fellow son of God, reflecting divine glory.|
Detailed Explanation of the Key Aspects:
1. The Truth (Abiding in the Word)
Ignorance: One who lives in agnosis is unaware of the divine Word, disconnected from the resonance of God's name and presence, and led by worldly knowledge.
Transitioning: The individual begins to acknowledge the Truth but struggles to maintain consistent focus. They hear God's voice intermittently but are often distracted by worldly concerns.

Gnosis: Living in constant awareness of God's truth, they abide fully in the Word, practicing the holy breath (Yah-Weh) and aligning with the divine vibration that reveals the reality of heaven within.
2. The Flow (Living in the Spirit)
Ignorance: They are disconnected from the divine flow, relying on personal will, and often experience chaos or stress without realizing the divine Spirit's guidance.
Transitioning: They experience the Flow in moments but struggle to sustain it consistently. They recognize the benefits but are easily pulled back into ego-driven actions.
Gnosis: They live in daily engagement with the Holy Spirit, connecting through the Flow, which calms and nourishes the soul. This inner peace leads to deeper discernment in all actions.
3. The View (Childlike Awareness)
Ignorance: They view the world through a materialistic lens, missing the divine presence behind creation and seeing life through the ego.
Transitioning: They begin to see the presence of God in moments but often revert to worldly perspectives, struggling to maintain spiritual clarity.

Gnosis: They cultivate a childlike awareness, humbling themselves and observing the divine hand in all things, free from intellectual interference. The Spirit effortlessly directs their thoughts and actions.
4. The Life (Spiritual Rebirth)
Ignorance: Dominated by ego, they resist surrendering their personal will to God, often struggling to control their experiences.
Transitioning: They practice surrender intermittently but return to striving and personal desires. They feel moments of spiritual rebirth but struggle to make it consistent.

Gnosis: They fully surrender to God's will, laying down their life each day, as Jesus said, "I lay down my life, that I might take it again" (John 10:17). This spiritual rebirth leads to renewed life, clarity, and alignment with God's presence.
5. The Way (Proper Prayer)
Ignorance: Their prayers, if any, are focused on personal gain, or they are disconnected from prayer entirely.
Transitioning: They begin integrating prayer but often focus on personal desires and struggle with trusting in God's timing.

Gnosis: They pray with sincerity and submission, aligning every word and intention with the Father's will. They start every prayer with the Lord's Prayer, synchronizing their breath with God's name (Yah-Weh) and trusting in His guidance.
6. The Hope (Hopeful Repentance)
Ignorance: They place their hope in worldly achievements, feeling lost and disconnected from divine perfection.
Transitioning: They experience hope in moments but fluctuate between doubt and trust, struggling to maintain a consistent vision of divine purpose.

Gnosis: They hold a forward vision of divine perfection, trusting that their repentance and faith will purify them. They meditate on their ideal state of being as already perfected, living in alignment with divine purpose.
7. The One (Righteous Perseverance Leading to Seeing God the Father Eternally)
Ignorance: Easily discouraged, they lack perseverance in seeking divine truth and turn to worldly distractions when faced with trials.
Transitioning: They demonstrate perseverance in some areas but inconsistently seek the revelation of Christ and God's will.

Gnosis: They steadfastly seek God's revelation, practicing the six principles daily. They receive the Holy Anointing, which confirms their spiritual unity and allows them to see God the Father clearly, knowing Him beyond belief.
8. The Law (Understanding Divine Law and Karma)
Ignorance: They ignore or break the commandments, leading to inner conflict, dissatisfaction, and disconnection from God's will.
Transitioning: They struggle with obeying divine law, slipping into old habits or temptations but trying to follow Christ's teachings.

Gnosis: They live in perfect harmony with the divine law, understanding that life is a mirror. As they manifest the law's unbreakable, unchanging nature, they experience divine wonders and greater revelations.
9. The Son (Becoming Like Christ)
Ignorance: They are disconnected from their identity as a child of God, acting from ego and unaware of their divine purpose.
Transitioning: They begin to recognize the calling to serve as a son or daughter of God but struggle with ego and attachments to worldly identity.

Gnosis: They meet Jesus Christ directly and understand what it means to be a fellow son of God. They embody Christ's words and actions, understanding, "When we see him, we will see him as he is; because we will be like him" (1 John 3:2). They fulfill their role in God's plan, knowing, "We shall judge angels" (1 Corinthians 6:3).

This comparison illustrates the spiritual progression from Agnosis (Ignorance), through Self-Gnosis (Awakening), to Gnosis (Divine Knowledge)—the ultimate attainment of unity with God's will and eternal truth.
C: The Fruits of Gnosis: Heaven's Requirements
*The principles are now reordered according to their color-coded seven spirits of revelation.
1. Abiding in the Word (The Truth): Red

Abiding in YHWH, the Word, is the foundation of spiritual life. Jesus said, "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth" (John 17:17, Ethiopian KJV). To be sanctified means to be set apart by the Truth, and that Truth is the resonance of God's name and presence. By continually abiding in the Word, we align ourselves with the Truth of God and free ourselves from illusions.

Abiding in the Word not only guides us to live in accordance with divine principles but opens a living relationship with God, where His presence permeates every breath we take. This alignment transforms the heart, purifies the mind, and sanctifies our being, allowing us to see the world through the lens of divine Truth.

The practice of abiding in the Word is inseparable from the name of YHWH. By invoking His holy name with our breath, we attune ourselves to the divine rhythm that aligns body, mind, and spirit with the eternal Truth. The name YHWH, spoken with the breath, is more than a word; it becomes a living experience that draws us deeper into communion with God.
Practical Step: Synchronizing with the Holy Breath of YHWH

To abide fully in the Word, we must practice synchronizing our breath with the sacred rhythm of YHWH. This breath practice is a way of aligning ourselves with the divine flow, creating harmony between the inner spirit and outward expression.

1. Inhale "Yah" through the mouth: Begin by inhaling with the sound of "Yah" for about a count of 6 seconds. The breath should be deep but relaxed, filling your lungs naturally without forcing or exaggerating the hold. The sound originates from the heart, collarbone, and throat area, not from the lips, tongue, or mouth itself. It is a natural sound, created when we fully relax and breathe correctly. There is a gentle, quiet pause at the top of the inhale, lasting for a moment as the breath fills your core.

2. Exhale "Weh" through the mouth: As you exhale for about 6 seconds, allow the breath to flow out completely. The sound of "Weh" should feel like a wave rushing to the shore of your physical body, washing over you. There is a subtle pause at the bottom of the exhale, as you feel the breath's release, fully grounded. This breath is complete—fully in and fully out, relaxed and easy.

3. Transition to the silent breath: Once the sound and rhythm are established, gradually move toward maintaining this breath with the mouth closed, allowing it to sound like the ocean. The inhales become the quiet retreat of the waves drawing inward to your core, while the exhales resemble the waves crashing gently against the shore, which is your physical body. As the practice progresses, the breathing becomes less exaggerated, softer, and more natural, mirroring the internal rhythm of peace and presence.

This breathing practice, starting with audible inhales and exhales, helps to make the connection between the Word and breath tangible. Once the natural rhythm is established, you move toward pure silence—an unstimulated state of being where the breath flows effortlessly. This shift reflects a deeper communion with God's presence, where even the sound of the breath becomes one with the silent Truth within.
The Three Core Gears of the Truth: External, Internal, and Eternal
The Word, like the breath of YHWH, moves through three stages: external, internal, and eternal. These represent the progression of spiritual alignment with God's Truth:

1. The External Word: Spoken aloud, the Word of God is expressed through the letter of the Truth—through Scripture, prayer, and spoken praise. This is the outward manifestation of the Word, bringing divine Truth into the physical world.

2. The Internal Word: As you focus inward, the Word becomes the spirit of Truth. It is no longer just spoken but begins to resonate within your heart and mind, creating a dialogue between you and God. This is where the Word moves from being an external guide to an internal reality.

3. The Eternal Word: The final stage of the Word is experienced in silent communion. Here, the Word transcends language and sound, becoming a silent, unbroken awareness of God's presence. This is the eternal Truth, the unspoken Word, where God's essence is breathed into every moment of your being.

By engaging all three aspects of the Word—external, internal, and eternal—you deepen your connection to the divine. The spoken Word keeps you grounded in God's teachings, the internal Word aligns your spirit with His, and the silent Word leads you into the eternal presence of God, where Truth is lived and breathed beyond words.
D: The Ocean Within: The Divine Mirror of Breath

The rhythm of this breath mirrors a spiritual truth: the ocean within reflects the ebb and flow of life and Spirit. As the waves of the ocean rise and fall, so does the breath carry the Word within us. Our flesh is the shore, where the Spirit touches and interacts with the world, and through this breath, we become conscious of the divine flow.

By practicing this breath of YHWH, we align ourselves with the natural rhythm of the Spirit, and as we enter the silent breath, we move toward deeper spiritual awareness. The breath becomes an anchor, grounding us in the Truth, and connecting us to the oceanic depth of God's eternal presence.

This breath practice allows you to hear the Word within, creating a space for silent communion with God. The Word is not only spoken; it is lived, breathed, and known at the deepest level of your being. Through this practice, you experience the Truth as a living reality, sanctifying you in body, mind, and spirit.

By continuously aligning with the holy breath of YHWH, you become a vessel of divine Truth, bringing forth the Word in all that you think, speak, and do. Living in this Truth opens the way for greater communion with God and a life that reflects His eternal Word.
2. Living in the Spirit (The Flow): Orange

Living in the Spirit is about engaging with the Flow of divine life, as exemplified by Jesus when he said, "The words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life" (John 6:63, Ethiopian KJV). This Spirit flows in the breath of life that turns into the life of breath—an inner source that nourishes eternally. Jesus alluded to this divine wellspring when he said, "Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst" (John 4:14, Ethiopian KJV).

The difference between the breath of life and the life of breath is profound. The breath of life refers to the initial, unconscious rhythm that sustains the body. The life of breath, on the other hand, is the conscious engagement with the Spirit—the eternal flow within the breath that nourishes the soul, calming and steadying it in divine peace. This is the wellspring of eternal life, the waters that cause us to neither hunger nor thirst.
The Practice of Ujjayi Breath: the Breath of Life - to - the Life of Breath

The Ujjayi Breath is the gateway to experiencing this Flow. It involves constricting the throat slightly during exhalation, creating a rasping sound, and focusing on the relief felt upon exhaling. However, the breath itself is not the destination; it is only the starting point. The true essence lies in following the feeling—the alternating sensations of ease and calm that arise beneath the breath.
Steps to Engaging the Flow:
1. Inhale through the nose: Expand the ribcage gently, not forcing the breath. Pause at the top, letting pressure build slightly.
2. Exhale slowly: Use the Ujjayi technique, creating the "Ahhh" sound at the back of the throat.
3. Follow the feeling of relief: Do not let your focus return to the physical sensation of breathing. Instead, allow your awareness to remain on the relief that the exhale produces.

4. Shift focus to the alternation: Notice how relief transitions into calm as you inhale, and back into deeper ease on the exhale. Keep your attention anchored in this Flow—this is the Spirit of the Word in action.

Practical Step: As you follow the Flow, allow it to become self-sustaining, independent of your focus on the breath itself. The Flow deepens as it alternates between ease and calm, revealing the Spirit's presence within every breath ​.
3. Childlike Mindset (The View): Yellow

Jesus emphasized the need for a childlike mind to enter the kingdom of heaven: "Whosoever shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 18:4, Ethiopian KJV). This childlike state embodies humility, innocence, and openness, qualities that allow us to experience the divine with clarity. The View is the state of pure awareness, or more specifically, aware-awareness—a heightened state of being where our awareness becomes conscious of itself. This experience is like a mirror, where our light is reflected off God and returned back to us, producing an inner shift in knowing.

In the View, there is a direct encounter with our own awareness in its purest form. This reflection allows us to perceive the presence of God more fully, resulting in a subtle but profound internal shift. There is often an acute feeling associated with this moment—a realization that feels both immediate and transcendent. Yet, this experience cannot be forced. At first, all we can do is ask, observe, feel, and watch. Over time, we begin to recall this state after it happens, until eventually, we can meditate and rest in the View itself.
The Childlike Mind: Trusting and Observing

Like a child waiting for guidance, the childlike mind does not try to control the outcome. Instead, it shows up in trust and waits for direction. In the same way, when we ask for the View, we are not trying to force awareness but to observe it as it arises. We ask, and then we wait, trusting that God will reveal His presence through our own awareness.

As we observe this awareness, we begin to understand that it is not something separate from us; it is who we are. This realization deepens as we continue to meditate in the View, and over time, we recognize that we are not just witnessing awareness—we are the awareness. This shift from simply observing to being the View is the transition from being spiritually "asleep" to being spiritually awake.
Awareness Reflected Back: Seeing God in the View

The View is more than just a state of self-awareness—it is the place where we see God's reflection in our own light. As our awareness reflects off God, it is returned to us, illuminating both our inner being and the world around us. This reflection enables us to see God's hand guiding our actions and decisions in real time, especially when we show up to the situations or places we have prayed about, trusting in His direction and results.

In the View, we are not only aware of ourselves but also of how God is working through us. This guidance becomes clear when we enter situations with faith, having already prayed for direction. Just like a child waiting patiently for instruction, we wait in the View, trusting that God will guide us. When the View is fully realized, we see that God's hand is present in every decision and action.
The Inner Shift of Knowing

The moment of experiencing the View is often accompanied by a deep inner shift in knowing—an immediate understanding that transcends intellectual reasoning. This shift is a feeling of awakening, a recognition that we are no longer spiritually asleep but fully present and alive in the awareness of God's presence. It is as if we have moved from the shadows into the light, where everything becomes clearer and more vivid.

This state of knowing is not something that can be forced or manufactured. It comes naturally when we ask for it and allow ourselves to be open, humble, and receptive. At first, it may feel fleeting, but with practice, we can return to the View more frequently, until it becomes our natural state of being.
The Path to Meditating in the View

At the beginning, our task is simply to ask for the View and to be present enough to notice when it arises. We observe, feel, and see the shift in awareness when it occurs, and afterward, we recall it—bringing the memory of that state back into our consciousness. As we practice, we begin to recognize the patterns of the View and can eventually enter it more consciously and at will.

Meditating in the View means resting in this state of pure, aware-awareness. It is the place where we are fully awake, both to our own consciousness and to God's presence within and around us. In this state, we are no longer striving to understand or control; we are simply being in alignment with God's will.
Practical Step: Asking for the View

To cultivate the View, begin by asking yourself simple, profound questions like "Am I aware?" or "Who am I?" These questions cause the mind to pause, creating space for the awareness of God to arise. But remember, this is not an intellectual exercise—your goal is not to answer the question but to observe the shift in your awareness that follows.
● Ask: In moments of stillness, ask yourself, "Am I aware?" or "Who am I?" and allow the silence that follows to reveal the View.
● Observe: When the shift in awareness occurs, simply observe it. Don't try to hold on to it or manipulate it; just feel it and let it unfold naturally.
● Recall: After the experience, take time to reflect on it. Bring the memory of the View back into your awareness, and let it guide you in future moments of meditation and reflection.
The View as a State of Spiritual Awakening

Living in the View is living in a state of spiritual awakening. It is the transition from being spiritually asleep—lost in thought, distraction, or ego—to being fully present, alive, and connected to the aware-awareness that is the essence of our being. In this awakened state, we see God's presence in every aspect of our lives, guiding us with gentle precision and love.

When we live in the View, we become like children who trust in the care and direction of their Father. We no longer strive to control or manipulate our circumstances; instead, we trust that God is leading us. This trust allows us to live in peace, knowing that we are always in the right place at the right time, guided by the light of God's presence reflected back to us through our own awareness.

In this childlike trust, we come to understand that the View is not something external or separate from us—it is who we are. It is the place where we experience the fullness of God's love and guidance, and it is the key to living a life of faith, trust, and spiritual awakening.
4. Spiritual Rebirth (The Life): Green

Jesus highlighted the profound importance of spiritual rebirth when He said, "I lay down my life, that I might take it again. No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again" (John 10:17-18, Ethiopian KJV). This illustrates a deep willingness to submit our very essence—the "I," the source of our individuality—to the Father. To be reborn spiritually is to willingly lay down our own will and surrender it fully to God, much like the kings in Revelation who "cast their crowns before the throne, saying, Thou art worthy, O Lord" (Revelation 4:10-11, Ethiopian KJV). This surrender, and the act of rebirth, aligns us with the flow of God's will and brings us into a renewed life of divine power.

Spiritual rebirth first begins by asking the Holy Spirit to enter your heart and bring new life in the name of Jesus Christ and God the Father. However, we do not pray to the Holy Spirit. All prayers are directed to God the Father alone. God has power, and He has given us the ability to speak life and death, as the Scriptures say, "Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof" (Proverbs 18:21, Ethiopian KJV). This power allows us to affirm our state of being with words—aligned with the Word of God—and see it come to pass. The act of rebirth is a continual process, requiring daily submission and surrender.

Whenever our will tries to overtake us out of habit, we must die to self and be reborn. This process is similar to the phoenix, which knows it must burn and endure pain but rises again. The phoenix does not flee from the inevitable, nor does it revel in the suffering—it holds faith through persistence and is reborn in a new form, just as Jesus endured the cross. Jesus reminds us that "the light of life" (John 8:12, Ethiopian KJV) flows from our attention, and that "If therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light" (Matthew 6:22, Ethiopian KJV). To lay down our life is to lay down our light, trusting that God will return it to us brighter and purer than before.

Spiritual rebirth is like letting go of the "self" and experiencing the process of being cleaned from within. God removes the dirt from our souls, returning our light clearer than before. It's like suddenly waking up refreshed after a deep sleep, and the burdens that once weighed us down disappear, leaving peace and clarity.
Practical Step:
Go into private, silent meditation for 15-20 minutes each morning with no intention or desire to control the experience. Begin with the declaration:

"As I sit here, I voluntarily submit all efforts to control or direct my personal experience with awareness or intention. I may move, adjust, think, or reflect, so long as I do not willingly do so. If it happens, it is meant to happen; if it doesn't, it is meant not to happen. I am like a passerby, watching all thoughts and sensory phenomena pass me by. I do nothing, intend nothing, try nothing. I non-do. I be. I AM. Amen."

In this state of non-intention, surrender your life and will to God. Allow the Spirit to work through you, like the dirt in a glass of water that settles to the bottom when the stirring stops. As you let go of attention and intention, clarity will naturally arise. This practice is a daily rebirth, where you continually die to self and rise anew, purer and clearer in the light of God's presence.
5. Proper Prayer (The Way): Blue

Proper prayer is the foundation for aligning our hearts and minds with the Father's will. Jesus provided clear instruction on how to pray effectively, saying, "When thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret" (Matthew 6:6, Ethiopian KJV). This emphasizes private, sincere communication with God, where we open ourselves to His guidance and submit our desires to His divine will.

Prayer is not just about the words we speak; it is the condition of our hearts, our willingness to surrender, and our trust in God's provision. Jesus exemplified this in His own prayer life, teaching us to say "Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven" (Matthew 6:10, Ethiopian KJV). This submission to God's will is essential for effective prayer.
The Lord's Prayer as the Introduction to Proper Prayer

The Lord's Prayer, given by Jesus as the model for all prayer, contains the essential elements of approaching God: reverence, surrender, trust, and seeking His guidance. We begin all prayer with this introduction:
1. Address the Father: Start by acknowledging God's holiness:
"Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name" (Matthew 6:9, Ethiopian KJV).
This recognition of God's divine nature sets the tone of reverence and submission.
2. Surrender to God's Will:
Declare that His will be done in your life and the world around you:
"Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven" (Matthew 6:10, Ethiopian KJV).
This is the heart of proper prayer—seeking alignment with God's perfect plan.
3. Trust for Provision:
Ask for what you need, but trust in His timing and wisdom to provide:
"Give us this day our daily bread(or meat/manna)" (Matthew 6:11, Ethiopian KJV).
We must approach with faith that God knows our needs before we ask.
4. Seek Forgiveness and Guidance:
Confess your sins and seek the strength to forgive others:
"And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors" (Matthew 6:12, Ethiopian KJV).
Aligning with forgiveness clears your heart for true communion with God.
5. Request Protection from Evil:
Finally, seek protection from the spiritual forces that lead us astray:
"And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil" (Matthew 6:13, Ethiopian KJV).
This is a reminder to trust in God's guidance and protection as you move through life.
The Ingredients of Effective Prayer

True prayer requires several key elements, each of which plays a critical role in the process of aligning with God's will. These ingredients help ensure that your prayers are effective and grounded in the right spirit:
1. Reverence for God

Begin every prayer with deep respect for God's holiness. Acknowledge His power, wisdom, and love. This reverence prepares your heart to receive His guidance and aligns your spirit with His divine presence.
2. Submission and Surrender

Proper prayer involves surrendering your will and desires to God's higher plan. Jesus demonstrated this when He said, "Not my will, but thine, be done" (Luke 22:42, Ethiopian KJV). In every prayer, you should express your willingness to submit to God's will, even if it means letting go of your own plans.
3. Faith in God's Provision

Believing that God has already heard your prayer and is working on your behalf is essential. Jesus said, "What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them" (Mark 11:24, Ethiopian KJV). This faith turns prayer into an active expression of trust.
4. Alignment with God's Will

True prayer seeks to align with God's purpose. You are not merely asking for things that serve personal interest, but you are looking to fulfill God's will in your life. Ensure that your prayers are focused on the greater good and seek to manifest His kingdom on earth.
5. Forgiveness and Reconciliation

Forgiveness is crucial for maintaining a pure heart during prayer. Jesus linked the effectiveness of our prayers with our ability to forgive others: "And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses" (Mark 11:25, Ethiopian KJV). Forgive to clear any blockages between you and God.
6. Persistence in Prayer

Jesus taught us to persist in prayer, saying, "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you" (Matthew 7:7, Ethiopian KJV). Proper prayer is not a one-time event—it's a continual act of seeking, asking, and knocking. Persistence shows faith and determination in your relationship with God.
7. Silent Reflection and Listening

After speaking, allow time for silent reflection. Prayer is not only about asking; it is also about listening. Silent moments in prayer create space for God's wisdom to enter your heart. As you sit in stillness, God's voice will begin to guide you.
Proper Prayer Techniques: Synchronizing Breath with the Divine

To further align with God's presence during prayer, Jesus instructed us to connect to the breath, the rhythm of life. This is where the sacred breath of YHWH comes into play. Breathing in sync with the name of God—inhale on "Yah," exhale on "Weh"—attunes your spirit to His presence. This act of breathing His name brings you into the divine flow of energy, helping you maintain focus and surrender.
Practical Step:
1. Start each prayer session with the Lord's Prayer as a foundation, fully engaging with its meaning.
2. Afterward, begin silent prayer, synchronizing your breath with the name of God—inhale "Yah," exhale "Weh."
This breath serves as a reminder that you are one with God's life force, and it will center you during your prayer, creating a calm, focused atmosphere for divine communication.
Practical Step for Daily Prayer
1. Start your day in private prayer: Find a quiet place (ideally your closet, like Jesus said), shut the door, and begin with the Lord's Prayer,

"Our Father who art in Heaven, holy hallowed be thy Name(YHWH), thy Kingdom Come, thy will be done, in Earth as is in Heaven. Please give us this day, our daily bread (that i AM). And forgive us our sins as we forgive those who sin against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil, for thine is the kingdom, the power and the glory, forever and ever." Let this serve as your introduction, aligning your heart and intentions with God's will.

2. Focus on specific, intentional or holy requests: First, pray, "Father, what would ye will that I pray unto thee?" Why? The Father already knows what you need before you ask him. So, if you ask to do his will, he will supply your needs automatically in respect to asking to do what He Wills you to ask and do. Within this process of self-prayer, then pray for your closest loved ones, and then branch out from there.

3. Keep a prayer list: When you meet new people, add their names to the list each day. If you learn something specific about them, pray in regard to that area of life. Otherwise, when you mention them by name in your Lord's Prayer, you are spreading the Father's mercy to them and their families. Without this, a man's karma will inevitably come for him, but mercy allows the Father to delay a man's punishment unto salvation.

4. Pray with purpose: Notice how The Lord's Prayer begins as, "Our Father…" and "Forgive us…," and "Give us…," and "Keep us…" This means we should be praying for our friends, family, associates and even our enemies, mentioning them by name.

5. Avoid vague or repetitive words: Let each request be unique or rooted in the basic, filled with meaning, and in alignment with God's higher plan: "May each of us come to ever know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou has sent."

6. Breathe in rhythm with God's name: As you pray, synchronize your breath with "Yah" on the inhale and "Weh" on the exhale when you need to take a breath. This will bring your spirit into alignment with God's presence, deepening your connection to the divine.

7. End with silent reflection: After speaking your prayer, remain in silence for several moments, open to receiving guidance from the Father. This period of stillness allows for divine wisdom to flow into your heart. This is also the best time to begin reading proverbs each day, over and over again. Read out loud. Put the wisdom on your lips.

8. Carry the prayer throughout your day: The effectiveness of prayer extends beyond the moment you finish. As you go about your day, keep your heart in a state of prayer by remaining open, focused on God's will, and trusting in His provision by proceeding directly into your morning meditation practice.

By incorporating these ingredients and techniques, you will find that your prayers lead to tangible, real-world results. Your heart will become increasingly aligned with God's will, and you will begin to see His guidance and blessings manifest in your life.
6. Hopeful Repentance (The Hope): Indigo

Repentance is a core element of aligning with divine perfection, and it is crucial to understand the difference between repenting from sin and repenting from mistakes. For a saved soul, repentance is primarily about correcting mistakes—misalignments or errors in judgment, which are part of human imperfection. In contrast, for the unsaved soul, sin is the denial of Christ, the rejection of truth, and the refusal to acknowledge divine will. Jesus emphasized this distinction when He said, "Of sin, because they believe not on me" (John 16:9, Ethiopian KJV). For the unsaved, sin is rooted in unbelief, whereas for those walking the path of salvation, sin is about straying from the alignment with God's will.

True repentance is not a mere apology or acknowledgment of wrongdoing. It is a conscious return to the path of righteousness—a realignment with God's divine will and a rejection of all that separates us from Him. As Scripture tells us, "Every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure" (1 John 3:3, Ethiopian KJV). This purification comes from hope—the forward-looking vision of our perfected state in God.
The Nature of Hopeful Repentance

Hopeful repentance isn't simply a backward glance at our sins or mistakes, but a forward movement toward divine perfection. Repentance with hope means acknowledging our errors while focusing on the purity we are becoming. It's the act of shifting away from human flaws and toward God's intended vision for us—His divine blueprint.

When we truly repent, we do so with a hopeful heart, confident that the act of turning away from mistakes and focusing on our higher calling will bring us into alignment with God's will. This isn't wishful thinking; it's active faith. Hope becomes the driving force behind repentance, fueling our ability to grow and purify ourselves. Just as a gardener removes weeds from a plant to give it room to flourish, repentance clears the space for our soul to grow toward divine light.
Hope as a Vision of Perfection

In practical terms, hope is the vision of ourselves already aligned with the perfection God desires for us. It is not merely about imagining a better version of ourselves—it's about embracing that state of being as if it already exists. This is the difference between fantasy and faith: fantasy is detached from reality, while faith holds the potential to manifest in our present life. Hopeful repentance uses faith to actualize this purified vision of ourselves, enabling our daily actions, thoughts, and circumstances to shift in alignment with that ideal state.
The Power of First-Person Perspective

When engaging in hopeful repentance, it's essential to take on a first-person perspective of your ideal, purified self. This perspective shifts your focus from seeing yourself as a flawed, struggling individual to seeing yourself as already purified, walking in divine perfection. It is not about faking or forcing a change but about embodying the truth that is already within you—waiting to be fully realized.

This shift from external hope to internal realization is crucial. By holding this vision of your perfected self in meditation, you allow your thoughts and actions to begin mirroring this state of purity. As you align with this vision, you will notice that your inner life shifts first, followed by external changes. You will start to think, speak, and act in ways that reflect the vision of divine perfection you've been holding.
Practical Step:

1. Hold the Vision: Begin by meditating on a first-person perspective of yourself in a state of perfection. See yourself already aligned with purity, walking in holiness, and fully connected to God's will. This isn't about imagining a distant future—it's about realizing that this state of being is available to you now. Envision yourself living in perfect alignment with divine love, truth, and light.

2. Dwell in the Vision: As you continue to meditate on this vision, allow it to become more real. Picture yourself thinking, speaking, and acting as though this state of perfection is your current reality. Let your mind naturally dwell in this space until it feels as though you are already living it. This could take some practice, but with persistence, the shift will become more natural.

3. Act from the Vision: Over time, as you hold and dwell in this vision, you will begin to notice spontaneous shifts in your daily life. You may find that your thoughts are purer, your actions more aligned with divine will, and even external events start to reflect this inner transformation. This is the practical application of hope: living in alignment with the purified state of being you are becoming, moment by moment, beyond the meditation practice.

4. Manifestation of Hope: The transition between simply seeing the act of perfection and living as if that perfection were already true is subtle but powerful. When your hope is fully aligned with the state of being you are hoping for, your actions, both within and beyond your active meditation, will naturally persist throughout your day. You will start to notice that your life unfolds in alignment with this perfected state, as if the hope itself has become reality.
The Role of Spontaneous Manifestation

As your hope becomes grounded in faith and action, you will begin to experience spontaneous manifestations of this perfection in your life. You will no longer just hope for alignment with divine will—you will live it. Repentance, then, becomes an ongoing process of refining and purifying, but it is always forward-looking, always rooted in the hope of divine perfection. These spontaneous events confirm that you are on the right path, that your hope and actions are aligned with God's will, and that divine transformation is happening within you and around you.
By embracing this practice, you allow the energy of hope to reshape your life, guiding you toward divine perfection, moment by moment, through the power of repentance and faith.
7. Righteous Perseverance (The One): Violet

Perseverance in righteousness is not simply about persistent effort but about enduring in the pursuit of divine truth until the full revelation of God the Father is experienced. Jesus taught, "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you" (Matthew 7:7, Ethiopian KJV). The spiritual journey requires ongoing dedication to prayer, study, and alignment with God's will through all six principles—The Truth, The Flow, The View, The Life, The Way, and The Hope. Only by living these principles do we begin to unlock the final mystery: the revelation of God the Father.
The Role of Righteous Perseverance

The core of righteous perseverance is in continuously seeking the revelation of Christ and the knowledge of God. This involves aligning every thought, word, and action with the divine flow, trusting that, in His time, God will reveal Himself. It is essential to practice The Truth, The Flow, The View, The Life, The Way, and The Hope daily, making them a part of every moment.

But when and where the full revelation of God the Father occurs is beyond our control. Only God knows the moment He will reveal Himself, and it happens in His timing. When the dawning comes, it will be right in front of you, undeniably clear, transcending all belief. There will be no need for more striving, effort, or understanding. This eternal knowledge, once unveiled, is like a light that never fades, whether in the light of day or the darkness of night. It is a knowing that transcends concepts, deeds, or even belief itself.
The Revelation of God the Father: The Author's Experience

For the author, the dawning of God the Father happened suddenly. In less than a second, awareness shifted from behind the eyes, through the tongue, and into the heart. It was as though an empty sphere passed through the tongue, accompanied by a brief, tasteless sensation. And then, it was gone.

Once awareness settled in the heart, it became clear: God is here, not as a distant concept but as the emptiness all around, as infinite space itself. The author could suddenly see why the sky is referred to as heaven—it is where God's essence is most pure, unburdened by the density of matter. In this revelation, the understanding came that God the Father is emptiness itself. The term "sky daddy" now had a deeper, more spiritual meaning—pointing to the emptiness and vastness of God's being, which we constantly dwell within.

Unlike most experiences where we understand after reflection, God the Father is experienced as a knowing first. This knowing arrives before any mental understanding, and it is only afterward, through reflection, that the deeper layers of wisdom begin to unfold. This wisdom is revealed as you live and apply this newfound knowing to other areas of life. The realization that combining this wisdom with the Flow of God is the essence of eternal life comes naturally. The revelation itself is pure, undeniable, and eternal.
The Holy Anointing: Unlocking the Final Revelation

The Holy Anointing marks the confirmation of this revelation. The specific prayer for this anointing opens the way for the full manifestation of God the Father. It is through this anointing that the truth of God's presence is solidified, marking the culmination of all that has been practiced and sought.

The Practice of 1-6: Preparing for the Revelation

Practicing The Truth, The Flow, The View, The Life, The Way, and The Hope is essential for unlocking the seventh principle—Righteous Perseverance. By living these truths daily, you are creating the spiritual foundation necessary for the final revelation of God the Father to occur.
The Truth:

Continue to abide in the Word, centering yourself in the divine truth of God's name and vibrations throughout the day. Hear the ocean within and say the Father's name whenever your breathing depth or rhythm fades due to ignorance or reactions. Let the sound of the waves and the ocean within occupy the periphery of your attention while keeping your focus on the task at hand. With continuous practice, this becomes the Word of Power that invokes all these experiences via association. Initially, it's a task to explore and commit to as a daily practice, but soon, it becomes your natural state of being. This focus replaces incessant inner dialogue or distractions, integrating spiritual and mental experiences. In psychology, this principle is referred to as "what wires together, fires together," which applies to both spiritual and mental-biological processes.
The Flow:

This represents the dormant aspect of the Holy Spirit when it isn't actively discerning something for you. To experience this consciously, you must undergo the Holy Spirit rebirth. For those who have been reborn, the Flow is the well within you. Ensure you connect with it daily, practicing whatever is necessary to reconnect your awareness to the alternating ease and calm of the Flow. Some days, it will be instinctive and effortless; on other days, it may be more challenging. It can be particularly difficult to observe the Flow in highly stimulating environments like moving vehicles, hot yoga sessions, or saunas. After anointing, this experience becomes significantly more profound. Ultimately, The Flow requires direct exercise, and while the other principles link easily to the Truth, this one demands deliberate practice.
The View:

Cultivate a childlike awareness of God's presence and His emptiness—His hand in all things. Recognize that all things derive value from how they interact with the space appointed to them by God in relation to other things. However, if you fill their spaces with concrete, their value disappears. All things honor God and reflect His handiwork. It is our role, as those who abide in The View, to be a voice that speaks of what we witness. Just as Jesus sat on His Father's throne, so too are we promised to sit on Christ's throne—the View within the core of our being. The question is: Are you aware?
The Life:

Find a quiet place where you can sit perfectly still and undisturbed. Intend nothing. Allow your will to rest. Simply be. At first, this might feel uncomfortable, but if you persist, the content of your mind-body experience will begin to settle. Eventually, a peaceful inner and outer clarity will emerge. This practice symbolizes dying to self through non-action, surrendering our will, and allowing God's Will to flow. The reason this works is that God's Will is always present, just as God is always present. All we have to do is stop insisting that things go our way and let His Way lead us to better life experiences and outcomes.
The Way:

Pray with sincerity, submitting to God's will in all things. Allow His guidance to shape your decisions. Pray for what you need, want, and also for the needs of others. Understand that you seek these things in a way that will glorify God the Father, His Word, and His Son. When you are blessed, praise God (for doing it), praise His Word (for showing you He did it), and praise His Son (for revealing the Way to be blessed by God Himself)! Amen! Proper private prayer, knowing every aspect is covered, is the only way to be certain that your prayers are working.
The Hope:

Live with the expectation of divine perfection, trusting that your repentance and faith will bring about the ultimate fulfillment of God's plan. This is a practice of vision, imagining, and even stepping into a dream. As you hope, it will grow each day, and your vision will expand and change as your knowledge increases. Combine this with prayer, and God Himself can show you what to hope for each day.

When all these principles are practiced with dedication and sincerity, the stage is set for God the Father to make Himself known to you. His dawning will come, not through force or control but through surrender and faith.
Practical Step:

● Daily Focus on Infinite Space: As you practice the six principles, make a conscious effort to focus on the space right in front of you. This space is where the revelation of God the Father will occur. Infinite space is God's eternal being, and as you meditate on this emptiness, you are preparing yourself for His dawning.

● Surrender and Wait for God's Timing: Trust that God will reveal Himself in His perfect time. When He does, it will be as if a light has been turned on, illuminating a truth beyond all belief. This knowing, once received, becomes an eternal presence in your life, guiding you in all things.

● Observe and Apply the Knowing: After the revelation, your awareness will be transformed. You will understand why the sky is heaven and why God's essence is emptiness itself. Apply this knowing to your life, and as you live in the flow of this truth, wisdom will unfold in new areas of your experience.

Through practicing The Truth, The Flow, The View, The Life, The Way, and The Hope, and focusing on the infinite space around you, the revelation of God the Father will occur. When and where this happens is up to God, but rest assured that it will be unmistakable. His eternal presence will be known to you, transcending all belief and understanding. This is the ultimate goal of righteous perseverance, the final anointing that marks the fulfillment of your spiritual journey.
8. Living by Divine Order in and as Love (the Law): Pink (blind)

Jesus emphasized the importance of living in alignment with the divine law, encapsulated in the greatest commandment: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself" (Matthew 22:37-39, Ethiopian KJV). This commandment forms the foundation of The Law—the divine order that governs not only our relationship with God but also our relationship with others.

The Law is the reflection of God's will, the universal principle that shapes and upholds all creation. It calls us to live righteously, in harmony with God, ourselves, and the world. In its perfection, the Law is both simple and profound: do unto others as you would have them do unto you, because life mirrors our actions, thoughts, and intentions back at us.

Understanding the Law means recognizing that our lives are guided by karmic principles, in which our deeds, words, and thoughts return to us as reciprocal experiences. The Law teaches us that what we give out—whether love or judgment, kindness or cruelty—will return to us in equal measure. Karma is not punishment or reward but the reflection of our being, constantly guiding us toward greater understanding and purity of heart.
The Perfection of the Law: Reflecting God's Will

The deeper we live in alignment with the Law, the clearer it becomes. Through loving God and others, we attune ourselves to God's will and move toward perfection. This perfection is not about legalistic adherence to rules but about embodying the spirit of love and righteousness in everything we do. The Law teaches us to act not out of obligation but out of the love that springs naturally from knowing God.

Jesus embodied the Law in its perfection, teaching that love fulfills all commandments: "On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets" (Matthew 22:40, Ethiopian KJV). His life and teachings show us that living by the Law of love brings about a profound transformation—both in ourselves and the world around us. When we act in accordance with divine love, we become vessels of God's presence, manifesting His will on earth.
The Mirror of Karma: Life Reflects Back Our Being

Living in alignment with the Law also means accepting that life is a mirror. Every action, thought, and word reflects our state of being and comes back to us, creating our lived reality. If we give love, we will experience love. If we act out of fear, anger, or selfishness, those emotions will be reflected back to us in various ways.

This understanding brings clarity to the golden rule: do unto others as you would have them do unto you. Not only does this principle guide us toward compassionate and ethical behavior, but it also shows us that we are actively shaping our future through the way we treat others. The Law is the mechanism by which our inner state manifests outwardly, bringing either blessings or suffering, depending on the purity of our heart and actions.
In essence, living by the Law aligns us with the divine order of the universe, allowing us to experience the harmony, peace, and joy that come from being in tune with God's will.
The Law's Perfection: Manifesting Wonders

When we live the Law fully, we begin to experience the perfection of God's will manifesting in our lives in miraculous ways. As we become purer in heart and clearer in our intentions, the Law becomes more apparent to us, and we witness its perfection in action. This is where we see the Hope—our faith in God's unbreakable, unchanging Law—transform into the knowledge of its truth.

With this knowledge comes the ability to manifest great wonders, not through our power but through our alignment with the divine. Jesus promised that we would do greater works than He did: "He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do" (John 14:12, Ethiopian KJV). These greater works are the natural result of living in harmony with God's will, where the Law becomes a channel through which the divine flows into the world.

To live by The Law in prayer is to actively cultivate harmony by increasing good, reducing harm, sustaining what aligns with God's will, and eliminating what detracts from it. Through mindful prayer, we ensure that our requests align with God's will for both personal and collective good.

As Jesus said, "Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven" (Matthew 16:19, Ethiopian KJV). This means that by consciously binding harmful thoughts or actions, we limit their influence in both our lives and the world. At the same time, by loosing qualities such as love, compassion, and forgiveness, we open ourselves to their growth within and around us.

As we bind and loose, we are also called to forgive and bless others, seeing the best in them. This intentional goodwill allows others to change, as our prayers become a supportive force for their growth. In doing so, we experience how our will, aligned with God, can profoundly affect those willing to unite with us in spirit. Jesus affirmed this in saying, "If two of you shall agree on earth as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven" (Matthew 18:19, Ethiopian KJV). When our intent is united with others in mutual love and prayer, its power multiplies, reshaping both our lives and theirs.

As we continue to apply The Law in this way, hope matures into a knowledge of God's unbending law: as within, so without. This means that our inner spiritual alignment with love, truth, and forgiveness directly impacts our external reality. The more we commit to cultivating inner harmony, the more our outer world reflects heaven's grace and peace.
Practical Step: Applying The Law in Prayer

In prayer, start by focusing on the good already present in yourself and others, giving thanks and asking for these virtues to grow. Then, look at areas where negativity or discord has taken root and consciously bind these in prayer, seeking divine strength to reduce and eliminate them. At the same time, loose qualities of love, patience, and forgiveness within your heart, and pray that these virtues spread outward to bless your relationships. As you forgive and bless others, see them in their best light, and trust that your prayers contribute to their positive transformation.

This process makes prayer a continual refinement of self and spirit. As we align our hearts and minds with God's law of love, we experience the fruits of true harmony, bringing forth a heaven within that radiates outwardly, enriching all that we touch.
Practical Step: Living by the Law

To live by the Law, begin each day by asking yourself how you can embody God's love in your interactions with others. Reflect on the golden rule: "Do unto others as you would have them do unto you" (Luke 6:31, Ethiopian KJV). Let this principle guide your thoughts, words, and actions throughout the day, knowing that whatever you give will be reflected back to you.
● Love First: In every encounter, ask yourself, "How can I love this person as I would want to be loved?"
● Act with Integrity: Make decisions that align with righteousness, even in difficult situations, knowing that living by the Law brings you into harmony with God's will.
● Reflect on Karma: Recognize that life mirrors your inner state. If you want to experience peace, joy, and love, cultivate those qualities within yourself and express them outwardly.

● Make Inner Effort: Each day, consciously bind harmful thoughts and actions that stray from God's love, and loose love, forgiveness, and peace within yourself. As you align your inner world with divine principles, trust that these actions will manifest in your outer life, bringing heavenly harmony to earth.

As you practice living in alignment with the Law, you will begin to see its perfection unfold in your life. Trust in the divine order, and know that by living according to God's will, you are participating in His eternal plan, bringing heaven to earth through your every action.
9. The Son's Perfection: Meeting Christ and Reflecting His Glory: White

The ultimate fulfillment of living by the Law is the realization of our identity as sons and daughters of God. Jesus promised that when we see Him, we will see Him as He truly is, because we will be like Him: "Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is" (1 John 3:2, Ethiopian KJV).

Living in the perfection of the Law leads to this divine transformation. When we align ourselves fully with the will of God and reflect His love and righteousness in our actions, we are made like Christ—pure, holy, and complete. As sons and daughters of God, we are called not only to live by the Law but to judge angels and participate in the divine governance of creation: "Know ye not that we shall judge angels?" (1 Corinthians 6:3, Ethiopian KJV).

Living by The Law is about aligning your heart, mind, soul, and strength with God's will, as Jesus taught: "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength... and love your neighbor as yourself" (Mark 12:30-31, Ethiopian KJV). This alignment reflects the truth that heaven is not just an external reality, but something within each of us.

Jesus also said, "Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven" (Matthew 16:19, Ethiopian KJV). This reveals that by binding and loosing—controlling our inner thoughts, beliefs, and intentions—we can influence not just our inner reality but also how it manifests externally. What is within affects what is without. If we bind negative thoughts or behaviors, we restrict them from influencing our life; if we loose divine love and truth within, we open ourselves to their flow in the world.

The Law teaches us that "as within, so without." Our inner heaven—our intentions, conscience, and alignment with love—directly impacts the external world. The more we align our inner life with love and truth, the more our external reality will reflect heaven's harmony.
E: Prayer and Communion with God

Prayer is foundational to deepening one's relationship with God, connecting us to His will and enabling us to live according to His divine purpose. Jesus taught His disciples the importance of prayer, saying, "But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly" (Matthew 6:6, Ethiopian KJV). Through prayer, we open ourselves to the voice of the Father, aligning our will with His. In this act of communion, we find guidance, strength, and the assurance of His presence.

Prayer, however, is more than just words; it is an act of submission and obedience to God's will. Jesus consistently demonstrated this in His own life, retreating to pray in solitude (Luke 5:16) and teaching us the Lord's Prayer, which emphasizes both God's holiness and the priority of His will on earth as it is in heaven (Matthew 6:9-13). To pray effectively, it is essential to follow Christ's example, praying not for personal desires alone but for alignment with God's kingdom and purposes. The Father listens to those who pray in obedience to the commands given by His Son, Jesus. As stated, "If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you" (John 15:7, Ethiopian KJV).
*The principles are organized below according to practical application, not revelation:
1. The Life: Surrendering in Prayer

Surrender is at the heart of true prayer, allowing us to fully enter into God's presence without the burden of trying to control or manipulate the outcome. Jesus exemplified this ultimate surrender in the Garden of Gethsemane when He prayed, "Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done" (Luke 22:42, Ethiopian KJV). In this moment, He expressed both His human desire to avoid suffering and His perfect submission to the Father's will. This moment of surrender is not only a model for how we are to pray, but also a profound revelation of what it means to trust God completely.

Surrendering in prayer means releasing all efforts to impose our own desires, expectations, or plans upon God. It is about letting go of control and allowing God's will to flow through us, even when we may not fully understand His plan. Jesus taught that the Father knows our needs even before we ask: "For your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him" (Matthew 6:8, Ethiopian KJV). Therefore, in prayer, we are not informing God of our needs, but aligning ourselves with His perfect provision and guidance.

In this state of surrender, we cease striving and enter a place of rest in God's presence. As the Author expresses in the proper prayer document, "To pray is to surrender control, sitting in silence, allowing the Spirit to move us instead of trying to force action." This kind of prayer invites the Holy Spirit to work within us, clearing away the clutter of our thoughts, fears, and anxieties, and making space for God's will to be revealed and manifest in our lives.
The Power of Non-Doing in Prayer

The concept of "non-doing" or non-action in prayer is rooted in the recognition that God is the ultimate actor, and our role is to yield to His movement. This non-doing is not passive or inactive; rather, it is a profound act of trust, where we allow God to guide the course of events without our interference. The more we surrender, the more we allow the fullness of God's will to flow through us. As Jesus said, "I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me" (John 5:30, Ethiopian KJV).

When we adopt this posture of surrender in prayer, we stop trying to control the narrative of our lives and instead open ourselves to God's divine wisdom and direction. This act of non-doing is itself an act of deep faith and reliance on God. It shifts the focus from what we can accomplish to what God is already accomplishing through us. It's the realization that our striving adds nothing to God's power and that His will, when allowed to unfold, brings about outcomes far greater than what we could imagine.
Sitting in Stillness: The Gateway to Clarity

Entering into a state of surrender during prayer requires creating space for stillness. Silence is not the absence of activity but the active presence of God, speaking into the quiet of our hearts. When we sit in stillness, free from distraction, without trying to control our thoughts or direct our experience, we create an opening for the Spirit to move. Jesus often withdrew to quiet, solitary places to pray, modeling the importance of stillness and silence in communion with the Father (Luke 5:16). In these moments of silence, clarity arises, not because we have solved our problems or figured out the right course of action, but because God's peace settles our minds and hearts, allowing His will to emerge.

The Author highlights this practice, saying, "By sitting in silent surrender, the mind settles, and clarity arises, allowing God's will to manifest through you spontaneously." This is where transformation happens—when we let go of trying to force solutions and instead allow the answers to emerge from God's presence. The act of sitting in silence for even 15 minutes can recalibrate our entire day, bringing us back to the center of God's will.
Practical Step: The Prayer of Surrender

To engage in the prayer of surrender, take 15 minutes daily to sit in stillness, releasing all efforts to control or direct the experience. Begin by affirming your intent to let go and allow God's will to work through you. The following prayer can help guide you into this state of surrender:
"I voluntarily submit all efforts to control or direct my experience. I do nothing, I intend nothing, I simply be. I AM. Amen."

As you sit, resist the temptation to direct your thoughts or focus on outcomes. Simply remain present with God, allowing any thoughts, feelings, or sensations to pass through without attachment. If your mind wanders, gently return to the intention of non-doing, resting in the assurance that God is at work even in the silence.

Over time, this practice of surrender will allow you to experience a deeper peace and trust in God's will. It cultivates an awareness of God's constant presence, leading to spontaneous moments of clarity and guidance. Jesus affirmed that true entrance into the kingdom of heaven comes through doing the will of the Father: "Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven" (Matthew 7:21, Ethiopian KJV). By surrendering to God's will, we position ourselves to receive and act upon His divine guidance.
Surrendering the Ego: Letting Go of Self-Will

One of the greatest challenges in prayer is the surrender of the ego—our desire to control, manipulate, and direct the outcomes of our lives. True surrender requires that we relinquish this self-will and place our trust entirely in God. This is not an easy task, as the ego often resists letting go, believing that it knows best. Yet Jesus teaches us that we must lose our self-centered life in order to find true life in God: "For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it" (Matthew 16:25, Ethiopian KJV).

In surrendering our ego, we recognize that God's ways are higher than our ways (Isaiah 55:9). This means accepting that His plans may not align with our immediate desires or understanding, but trusting that they are ultimately for our good and His glory. The practice of surrender is a continual process of releasing self-will and embracing God's will, knowing that He is shaping us into vessels of His divine purpose.
The Fruits of Surrender: Peace, Clarity, and Guidance

When we surrender in prayer, the fruits of peace, clarity, and divine guidance naturally follow. As we cease striving and rest in God's presence, His peace envelops us, quieting the mind and calming the heart. This peace, as Paul describes, "passeth all understanding" (Philippians 4:7, Ethiopian KJV), and it guards our hearts and minds, allowing us to navigate life with a deep sense of trust in God's direction.

Clarity is another fruit of surrender. When we stop trying to force outcomes, the solutions to our challenges often present themselves, not through our own reasoning, but through God's wisdom working within us. This clarity comes when we let go of our need to control and trust in God's perfect timing and provision.

Finally, divine guidance flows naturally when we surrender in prayer. As we open ourselves to God's will, He directs our steps, leading us in paths of righteousness for His name's sake (Psalm 23:3). Surrender positions us to hear and respond to His voice, allowing us to act in alignment with His plans.
Summary:

Surrendering in prayer is an act of trust, where we let go of control and allow God's will to work through us. Jesus modeled this surrender in Gethsemane, teaching us to pray, "Not my will, but thine, be done" (Luke 22:42, Ethiopian KJV). By practicing stillness and non-doing in prayer, we open ourselves to God's presence, allowing His peace, clarity, and guidance to flow through us.

The practice of daily surrender, sitting in silence and affirming, "I do nothing, I intend nothing, I simply be," helps quiet the mind and aligns our hearts with God's will. As we surrender our ego and self-will, we enter into a deeper trust in God's perfect plan, experiencing the fruits of peace and divine direction. Through this surrender, we become vessels for God's will to be done in our lives, fulfilling Jesus' teaching that only those who do the will of the Father shall enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 7:21, Ethiopian KJV).
2. The Truth: Aligning Desires with God's Will

Jesus' teachings emphasize that our prayers must align with the will of God. He taught, "Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven" (Matthew 6:10, Ethiopian KJV). In this divine truth, we learn that prayer is not about fulfilling our personal desires but about bringing our will into perfect harmony with God's eternal plan. When our desires align with God's will, our prayers become expressions of His truth. This brings forth a peace that surpasses understanding, knowing that God's will is perfect, and His provision is complete. Just as He provides for the birds of the air, so too does He provide for us when we abide in His truth: "Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?" (Matthew 6:26, Ethiopian KJV).

To align with God's will, we must realize that true prayer seeks what is righteous in God's sight, not what we imagine to be right from our limited perspective. As the Author reminds us, "To receive one thing is to give up another. True prayer seeks what is righteous in God's sight, not what we imagine to be right in our limited understanding." This requires spiritual discernment, a deep listening to God's voice, and a willingness to surrender our own will.
Abiding in YHWH: The Sound of the Ocean Within

To live in alignment with God's will, we must first learn how to abide in YHWH. Abiding means continuously dwelling in His presence, allowing His truth to permeate every aspect of our being.
